title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: ct_finish() runs geoms built, can inspect data. finds last point series drops dot name beside . Labelling lines directly replaces legend, example switches legend . ct_finish() normally widen x range make room labels, defers positional scale set rather replacing . example supplies scale_x_continuous() get integer year breaks, also supplies right-hand expand labels need.
code: library(ggplot2) library(ggconsulting) #> ✔ ggconsulting set ggplot2 aesthetic defaults #> ℹ Opt out: `ct_unset_defaults()` or `options(ggconsulting.autoload = FALSE)` #> ℹ Column width / linewidth: use `ct_col()` / `ct_line()`, or apply a #>   `theme_*()` archetype for linewidth via `from_theme()`  players <- subset(market_share, company != "Others")  ggplot(players, aes(year, share, colour = company)) +   ct_line() +   scale_colour_ct("strategy_navy") +   scale_y_continuous(labels = fmt_pct(decimals = 0)) +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = seq(2015, 2024, 3),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))   ) +   labs(     title    = "Player C gained nine points of share as the leader lost nine",     subtitle = "Share of category revenue",     x = NULL, y = NULL,     caption  = "Source: simulated data bundled with ggconsulting"   ) +   theme_strategy() +   theme(legend.position = "none") +   ct_finish(end_labels = TRUE, end_points = TRUE)

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: Data-aware finishing. ct_finish() runs geom layer built, one addition can add value labels, sort categories, highlight selected observations, label line endpoints, set geom-aware scale expansion. Portable locale formatting. ct_locale() fmt_*() helpers support pt-BR en-US without changing Sys.setlocale(). fmt_brl() keeps Brazilian Real formatting explicit, including accounting negatives. Theme-driven geoms. ct_theme() routes main colour linewidth ggplot2 4.x’s from_theme() mechanism, unmapped geoms inherit theme without extra scale calls. strategy, finance, editorial presets build theme system.

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: ct_theme() builds theme palette, font, density, context, paper. Three presets cover archetypes. theme_strategy() keeps minimal frame, generous whitespace, navy default. theme_finance() tightens spacing printed pages pitch books, drops gridlines, puts ticks y axis place. theme_editorial() sets serif face italic subtitle warmer palette. paper sets figure ground. Pass "cream", "warm_grey", "white", colour R recognises. theme_minimal() leaves panel blank, filling plot background alone produces uniform ground seam panel plot. Setting paper warms gridline match.  archetypes forward ... ct_theme(), theme_editorial(paper = "cream") works. Cream opt-rather editorial default.
code: ggplot(client_nps, aes(quarter, nps, colour = segment)) +   ct_line() +   scale_colour_ct("editorial_warm") +   labs(     title    = "Mid-Market sentiment caught up with Enterprise",     subtitle = "Net promoter score by client segment",     x = NULL, y = NULL,     caption  = "Source: simulated data bundled with ggconsulting"   ) +   theme_editorial(paper = "cream") +   theme(legend.position = "none") +   ct_finish(end_labels = TRUE)

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: ct_finish() reads built plot applies finishing moves otherwise make hand. can sort categorical axis value, highlight chosen categories muted rest, print value labels, label line endpoints, move y axis right, repeat y ticks opposite edge, expand scales suit geom.  highlight reads main colour theme, add theme ct_finish(). Reverse order highlights fall back hardcoded navy. end_labels also accepts "first_facet", pins every label first panel instead panel series happens end .
code: share_2024 <- subset(players, year == 2024)  ggplot(share_2024, aes(company, share)) +   ct_col() +   scale_y_continuous(     labels = fmt_pct(decimals = 0),     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))   ) +   labs(     title    = "The leader's advantage has narrowed to two points",     subtitle = "Share of category revenue, 2024",     x = NULL, y = NULL,     caption  = "Source: simulated data bundled with ggconsulting"   ) +   theme_strategy() +   ct_finish(sort = "desc", highlight = "Player A", values = TRUE, label_fmt = "pct")

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: Palettes come three families keyed archetypes, several options . Every palette holds six colours, first main colour ct_theme() routes element_geom(ink = ). ct_palette() returns palette’s colours, lists available names called arguments. scale_colour_ct() scale_fill_ct() map discrete data onto palette. interpolate warn data needs levels palette holds. scale_colour_ct_c() scale_fill_ct_c() cover continuous data, direction = -1 reverse. ct_palette_show() previews one palette, custom hex vector, every shipped palette . American British spellings exported.

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: ct_locale() switches active locale "pt-BR" "en-US" session. writes options(ggconsulting.locale) never touches Sys.setlocale(), output matches across Windows, Linux, macOS. package carries month names rather reading LC_TIME. fmt_number(), fmt_pct(), fmt_delta(), fmt_currency() follow active locale. fmt_brl() always renders Brazilian Real R$ non-breaking space whatever locale, takes style = "accounting" negatives parentheses. returns function, drop straight labels argument scale.

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: ct_col(), ct_line(), ct_point() wrap ggplot2 counterparts different defaults width, linewidth, size. Everything else passes . Attaching package also calls ct_set_defaults(), routes small set aesthetic defaults update_geom_defaults(). Turn options(ggconsulting.autoload = FALSE) loading, call ct_unset_defaults() mid-session restore ggplot2 originals. One gotcha carries ggplot2. ct_col()’s width counts x-axis units, Date axis means 0.8 days bars render slivers. Convert x factor index bar charts.

title: Executive-Grade Themes and Helpers for ggplot2
text: has_font() reports whether family available, checking installed session-registered fonts. install_consulting_fonts() fetches defaults Google Fonts. asks writing home directory unless options(ggconsulting.font_consent = TRUE) set. Themes degrade gracefully. ct_theme() walks font font_fallback takes first family present, missing Inter lands Helvetica Neue, Arial, generic sans rather failing.

code: ct_finish(   values = FALSE,   sort = NULL,   label_fmt = NULL,   highlight = NULL,   end_labels = FALSE,   end_points = FALSE,   axis_y = NULL,   mirror_y = FALSE,   expand = "auto",   muted_color = "#A8A4A0" )

title: Apply data-aware finishing touches to a plot — ct_finish
text: values TRUE adds value labels bars / next points. "auto" adds first geom column bar. sort One "asc", "desc", NULL. set, reorders factor levels x aesthetic y aesthetic. label_fmt Either formatter function (anything maps numeric vector character vector), one shortcut names "brl", "number", "pct", "delta" resolved matching fmt_*() helper. highlight Value(s) x aesthetic emphasise. Matching bars use active palette's main colour; non-matching bars use muted_color. Inserted scale_*_manual(). end_labels line plots: TRUE labels last point series group identifier. "first_facet" draws labels first panel, replaces legend across small multiples; unfaceted plot behaves like TRUE. x aesthetic may numeric, Date, POSIXct. end_points line plots: TRUE, draw filled point series' last observation, end label. axis_y Moves y axis. "right" "left"; NULL (default) leaves scale puts . Applied ggplot2::guide_axis(), disturb scale_y_*() call . mirror_y TRUE, repeats y-axis ticks opposite edge without labels, eye can track level across wide panel. Pairs gridline-free theme theme_finance(). Applied ggplot2::guides(), leaves scale_y_*() call alone. expand "auto" picks geom-aware scale expansion (room column tops, right-side room line end labels); FALSE disables. Auto expansion defers positional scale supplied , scale_y_continuous(labels = ) keeps labels; set expansion call need . muted_color Fill / colour used non-highlighted categories.

title: Locale-aware label formatters — ct_formatters
text: Factory functions: returns function compatible scales::label_* (callable numeric vector). Marks (thousands, decimals) currency symbols come active ggconsulting locale, set via ct_locale(). fmt_number() — plain numbers locale separators. fmt_brl() — Brazilian Real. Always renders R$ regardless active locale; locale argument lets override marks. fmt_currency() — uses active locale's currency symbol. fmt_pct() — percentages. default interprets input fraction (0.5 → "50%"); pass scale = 1 input already percent units (50 → "50%"). fmt_delta() — percentage-point-style signed deltas (+1,2pp / -0,3pp / 0,0pp). fmt_month() — Date / POSIXct → localised month string. Negatives default minus prefix; currency helpers also support style = "accounting", wraps negatives parentheses. Currency rendering uses non-breaking space (U+00A0) symbol number pair never wraps across lines.

title: Locale-aware label formatters — ct_formatters
code: fmt_number(decimals = 0, locale = NULL)  fmt_brl(decimals = 2, style = c("minus", "accounting"), locale = NULL)  fmt_currency(decimals = 2, style = c("minus", "accounting"), locale = NULL)  fmt_pct(decimals = 1, scale = 100, locale = NULL, accuracy = NULL)  fmt_delta(decimals = 1, suffix = "pp", locale = NULL)  fmt_month(format = c("abbr", "full"), locale = NULL)

title: Locale-aware label formatters — ct_formatters
text: decimals Number decimal places. locale Optional locale name. Defaults active locale. style "minus" (default) "accounting" currency. scale Multiplier applied input rendering, fmt_pct() . Defaults 100 (input fraction). Use scale = 1 input already percent units. accuracy Optional explicit accuracy passed scales::percent(); overrides decimals set. suffix Suffix fmt_delta(). Defaults "pp". format "abbr" (default) "full" fmt_month().

code: ct_theme(   palette = "strategy_navy",   font = "Inter",   font_fallback = c("Helvetica Neue", "Arial", "sans"),   density = c("normal", "tight", "loose"),   context = c("presentation", "report", "screen"),   base_size = NULL,   main_color = NULL,   paper = NULL )

title: Build a consulting-grade ggplot2 theme — ct_theme
text: palette Palette name (e.g. "strategy_navy") character vector colours. font Preferred font family. font_fallback Character vector fallback families try font unavailable. generic R families "sans", "serif", "mono" always recognised terminal fallbacks. density One "normal", "tight", "loose". Controls panel.spacing axis-text margins. context One "presentation", "report", "screen". Drives default base_size plot.margin. base_size Base font size. NULL, derived context. main_color Routed theme geom element's ink slot, unmapped geoms pick via from_theme(). NULL falls back palette's first colour. Title colour fixed neutral near-black (#1A1A1A); override follow-theme() call want palette-tinted. paper Figure ground colour. NULL (default) leaves ggplot2::theme_minimal()'s white background untouched. Otherwise one shortcuts "cream", "warm_grey", "white", colour grDevices::col2rgb() accepts. theme_minimal() leaves panel background blank, filling plot background alone gives uniform ground panel-versus-plot seam. Setting paper also warms major gridline match .

title: ggconsulting 0.1.0
text: Requires ggplot2 >= 4.0.0 R >= 4.1. themes built ggplot2 4.x API — theme_sub_*() helpers, element_geom(), from_theme() linkage — work ggplot2 3.x.

title: ggconsulting 0.1.0
text: ct_theme() composes theme palette, font, font_fallback, density, context arguments. palette’s main colour routed element_geom(ink = ...), from_theme()-aware geoms pick without explicit scale_color_*() call. theme_strategy() — minimal, generous whitespace, navy default. theme_finance() — serif preset (Source Serif 4 → Georgia → Times New Roman → serif) regular-weight title, lighter major gridlines, denser defaults (density = "tight", context = "report") tuned printed pages rather slides. Defaults finance_classic. theme_editorial() — serif preset italic subtitle larger, tighter-leaded title. Defaults editorial_warm. ct_theme(paper = ...) sets figure ground. Pass "cream" (Financial Times), "warm_grey" (Economist), "white", colour R recognises. theme_minimal() leaves panel background blank, filling plot background alone gives uniform ground panel-versus-plot seam. Setting paper also warms major gridline match. archetypes forward , theme_editorial(paper = "cream") works; cream opt-rather editorial default.

title: ggconsulting 0.1.0
text: Eleven palettes six colours , three families: five strategy (strategy_navy, strategy_emerald, strategy_crimson, strategy_azure, strategy_slate), three finance (finance_classic, finance_steel, finance_burgundy), three editorial (editorial_warm, editorial_clay, editorial_oxide). ct_palette() returns palette’s colours, subsets n, — called arguments — lists every available palette name. scale_color_ct() / scale_fill_ct() — discrete scales. data needs levels palette holds, colours interpolated warning points continuous scales instead. scale_color_ct_c() / scale_fill_ct_c() — continuous variants, direction = -1 reverse. British-spelling aliases: scale_colour_ct(), scale_colour_ct_c(). ct_palette_show() — swatch preview one palette, custom hex vector, every shipped palette faceted.

title: ggconsulting 0.1.0
text: ct_locale("pt-BR" | "en-US") — session-scoped locale switch stored options(ggconsulting.locale). touch Sys.setlocale(); package ships month tables formatting marks, output identical across Windows, Linux, macOS. fmt_number() — locale-aware numbers (1.234,5 / 1,234.5). fmt_brl() — Brazilian Real, always R$ non-breaking space regardless active locale. style = "accounting" wraps negatives parentheses. fmt_currency() — uses active locale’s currency symbol. fmt_pct() — fraction percent (0.5 → "50%"). fmt_delta() — always-signed percentage-point deltas (+1,2pp). fmt_month() — Date / POSIXct localised month string.

title: ggconsulting 0.1.0
text: value labels bars beside points (values = TRUE) reordering categorical x y (sort = "asc" | "desc") label formatting shortcut (label_fmt = "brl" | "number" | "pct" | "delta") user-supplied function highlighting specific x values theme’s main colour, muting rest muted_color (default #A8A4A0, warm-leaning neutral reads cool warm palettes) end labels last point line series (end_labels = TRUE), first panel faceted plot (end_labels = "first_facet"), replaces legend across small multiples filled point series’ last observation (end_points = TRUE) right-hand y axis (axis_y = "right"), applied guide_axis() leaves scale_y_*() call alone geom-aware scale expansion (expand = "auto") — headroom columns, right-side room line endpoints
